item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.5
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 5

One focused column. A meeting now opens as a single column with larger text, and the sidebar and toolbar step aside while you read. Press Escape to go back to Home. Settings, General, Show every place and button brings the full window back.

A simpler Home. Home is one page: your day first, then your notes grouped by date. Notes, People and Projects filter the list. The rest of the places are under More.

Flight is the look for everyone. New installs start in Flight, and anyone on Instrument is moved to it once. You can switch back in Settings, General, Look. Flight has a new manner: a calm, focused layout, with Decisions and Next Steps in one card that shows each step's owner and day, a time beside each line Tailwing wrote that opens the transcript at that moment so you can see where it came from, a day card on Home, and new icons and type.

Folio, a second look. Folio sets your notes on warm paper with serif titles and notes. It is free, and it is the second choice in Settings, General, Look.

Your day. Coming Up and This Week can show a day as well as a list, with a block for each meeting and a line that sums it up, such as how many meetings there are and when you next have an hour free. Next Steps now starts with Today and Upcoming. Quick Add, a small field for a to-do, is off until you choose a key in Settings, Shortcuts.

Share Notes. Share Notes in a meeting prepares a clean email of its notes, and Send Their Next Steps on a person's steps does the same for one person. You see exactly what will go and to whom, and you send it from your own mail app or copy it. Tailwing sends nothing itself. It is not offered for a private meeting.

Export Everything. Settings, Privacy, Your data, and the File menu, write your whole library to a new folder on this Mac. It never writes into or changes anything that was already in the place you choose.

AI tools that make changes. AI tools you have connected can suggest titles, speaker names, projects and folders, add their own notes and to-dos, flag moments, create a project, and ask Tailwing a question that comes back with links to the lines behind the answer. Each kind of change has its own switch in Settings, Connections, AI tools, and all of them are off until you turn on Let AI tools make changes. Suggestions wait under the meeting's title until you click Use, and Undo puts back what was there. For each tool you can also choose Apply without asking, which is off by default. A tool only changes or deletes items it added itself, and private meetings are never read or changed.

Faster, more trustworthy Ask. Answers appear as they are written, and each figure, quote and name is checked against the line it cites. Anything a line doesn't support is withdrawn.

Private meetings keep their owners. Notes for a private meeting are now written from what was said, before names are replaced, so next steps keep their owners and decisions keep their reasons. Only the replaced text is stored. A private meeting keeps no location.

A check on earlier private meetings. On a Mac that has had Pro, this release checks the private meetings you already have. Where an earlier version stored one without replacing names, Tailwing replaces them now and tells you how many meetings it changed.

Private meetings and sync. A private meeting's notes and audio stay on the Mac they were made on, and copies that earlier versions sent to iCloud are removed. If you sync between Macs, update all of them to this release: a Mac still on Beta 4 deletes its own copy of a private meeting's notes when another Mac removes them from iCloud.

Look up a person. On a person's page, Look Up fetches their title and organization from your own Apollo or Clay account. It appears only after you connect one in Settings, Connections, and it is part of Pro. Apollo is sent a name, an email address and the company's web domain, and Clay is sent a name and the company's web domain. Lookups use your own account and its credits.

Gift codes. Invite people from Settings, Invites, and you can earn up to three gift codes. Each code gives Pro on one Mac. To move a code to a new Mac, turn Pro off on the old one and enter the code on the new one in Settings, Pro, under Have a gift code?.

Live translation, where it keeps up. Live translation is offered only where it has been measured to keep up: the first words show within four seconds of a sentence starting, and the whole sentence about two seconds after it ends. Today that is English speech into Spanish, French, German, Italian and Portuguese. Every other language gets Translation after the meeting, with your notes written in your language. Spoken translation stops when you start talking.

  • A weekly count: once a week, one update check also carries a code that is different every week, so tailwing.co can count how many Macs use Tailwing. The code doesn't identify your Mac. It is on, and you can switch it off in Settings, Privacy, What leaves this Mac, Weekly count.

Settings and screen shares. When you share your screen, Tailwing hides Settings only on the panes that show people or text, so you can share the others.

Quitting. Command-Q asks whether to keep Tailwing in the menu bar so it can take notes for your next meeting. While a meeting is in progress it asks before it stops taking notes. You can set the answer once in Settings, General.

Fixes.

  • Dictation no longer quits the app when the microphone setup changes as it starts, such as when a dock or display is connected.
  • An AI tool sending an absurd number can no longer crash the app.
  • Side-panel text is no longer cut off at narrow widths.
  • The site and the app said Tailwing keeps each meeting's audio. Audio is deleted once the transcript and write-up are made, unless you choose to keep it in Settings, Privacy.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.4
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 4

Next Steps. A new page lists every open next step from all your meetings, yours first, with a checkbox on each. Ticking one here ticks it in the meeting and on its project page too. Press N to add a to-do of your own, and Command-Z undoes anything.

Decisions, as a page. Decisions now fill the page, with the reason, the meeting, who was there and the project. Filter by project, person, series or date, and open a decision in place to see the moment it was made.

Sources open where you are. The small numbers beside write-up lines are now a quiet mark. Click it to see who said it and when, under the line, with a link to the full transcript if you want it.

Dictation that keeps up. Pressing the dictation key while an earlier dictation is still being written starts listening at once, and the words arrive in order. A brief slip of the key, or another modifier key pressed while you hold it, no longer ends a dictation mid-sentence. A tap too short to hold speech is ignored quietly, and work on a finished call waits while you dictate.

Quieter on calls. Tailwing takes notes from the microphone your Mac has chosen, never one picked because another app was using it, and it no longer runs its own voice processing while a call app has the microphone. When devices change mid-call it switches once.

Calls end cleanly. A short call now stops by itself: Tailwing waits 20 seconds to be sure the call app has gone, then counts down. Notes are written as soon as a call stops, and a second call that starts straight after offers Continue or Start a New Meeting.

Your name, and theirs. You appear by your name in transcripts, decisions and next steps. A voice that couldn't be named reads as "someone" and never owns a step. Coming Up and This Week show people's names.

Projects that learn. With automatic sorting on, Tailwing learns which people and organizations belong to which project, and offers to give a recurring meeting a default project. Sorting is still off unless you turn it on in Settings, Meetings.

A note for the meeting chat. While Tailwing takes notes, Copy Note for the Chat puts a line on your clipboard that tells everyone, for you to paste. You can change the wording in Settings, Privacy.

Invite people. Invite Someone has your link, ready text for Messages, Mail and Slack, and a count of who joined. Bring in ten people and you become a founding member, with early access to betas.

Anonymize says what it did. A copied transcript now keeps each voice as its own speaker when it is anonymized, and Copy and Save tell you when names were removed. After an anonymized copy you can choose Copy Without Anonymizing for your own clipboard, unless the meeting is private.

Privacy in one panel. Settings, Privacy is now one list under Private mode, and each row is named for what its switch does. Settings no longer shift as you flip a switch.

Flight, redrawn. The Flight look has a new design: white cards on a warm off-white page, larger page titles, rounded pill buttons and a blue accent. Choose it in Settings, General. The other looks are unchanged.

Faster. Search no longer holds up typing, and the menu-bar menu opens at once.

Changed. Hearing translations spoken aloud is now part of Pro. If you already had it switched on, you keep it. Translated subtitles stay free.

Fixed. Settings and other windows open in front, including over a pinned window. The selected row in lists is readable in every look. Imports show what happened beside the button. The note that Tailwing is still running points at its menu-bar icon. The diagnostics log no longer includes microphone names.

Known issues. On a call played through speakers with no headset, some of what the other side says can be credited to you. If your own voice is split into several voices, your lines can read as "someone". "Someone" replaces an unnamed speaker in English write-ups only. With Anonymize on, some words that are not personal, such as product names, can still be replaced. Your own to-dos stay on this Mac and don't sync yet.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.3
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 3

A guided setup. Setup now introduces each feature, asks for the permissions it needs at that step, and shows what is downloading at the bottom of every screen. You can try dictation before you finish, and open a sample meeting to see what a write-up looks like. Everyone sees it once after updating; what you already allowed and downloaded shows as Ready, and your settings stay as they are.

A consent reminder before notes. Before Tailwing takes notes on a call, it asks you to confirm that you are responsible for getting consent from everyone you take notes with. Tailwing sends that confirmation to us once, with the date, the app version and an ID for your Mac, so it is on file. Dictation doesn't need it.

Ask shows what it will assume. As you type a question, Tailwing underlines the meeting, the dates and the people it will look at. Click one to change it before you send. Where it can't tell which meeting or person you mean, it asks instead of guessing, and each answer starts with what it was based on.

Decisions in one place. View, Decisions lists every decision across your meetings, newest first, with the reason given in the meeting and a link to the moment it was made.

Projects. Tell Tailwing about your most important projects in setup, or add them on the new Projects page. Each project collects its decisions, open next steps and meetings in one place, and you can ask a question about that project alone. Setup can also list your recurring meetings so you can say which project each belongs to, and you can mark a meeting as a project's anchor. Sorting items into projects automatically is off for now; you can turn it on in Settings.

How You Run Meetings. A new page beside Decisions shows your last four weeks against the four before: your share of talk time, the questions you asked, how often you started while someone was mid-sentence, your longest stretch and the cues you saw most. The suggestion under each meeting is now labeled Try Next Time. All of it stays on your Mac.

Links to a moment. Copy a link to any transcript line, source line or flagged moment. Opening it shows that line in the transcript. Exports and AI tools carry the same links.

Anonymize covers everything you save. With Anonymize on, names and personal details are now replaced in the notes you save, copy, share, drag out or send, including PDF and Markdown files and next steps sent to Reminders, Things and Todoist. If they can't be replaced, nothing is saved or sent.

Share and drag. Share a note from the macOS Share menu, or drag it to Finder or Mail.

Usage numbers, if you choose. Setup asks whether Tailwing may send counts about how it is working on your Mac, such as whether setup finished. It is off until you say yes, it never includes anything you say, write or dictate, and Settings, Privacy shows exactly what was sent. The same screen has an optional question about what you do for work. Your answer stays on your Mac unless you share usage numbers, and then it is sent as one of nine fixed choices.

Rate a dictation. Each item in your dictation history has Good and Not good buttons, and Not good lets you say what went wrong. Ratings stay on your Mac. If you share usage numbers, each rating is also counted with the kind of app and the language, and never the words or the audio.

Update checks are counted. When Tailwing checks for an update, our site counts the check with the app's version and build number, so we can see how many Macs are on each version. Nothing else is sent, and if that address doesn't answer, Tailwing checks the original one.

More at home on the Mac. Complete menus with the standard keys, a Help menu, spell check in notes, Settings that follow Increase Contrast, and a quiet start at login. The interface is now translated in the places that were still in English.

Better write-ups of long meetings. Write-ups no longer present something reported from a paper or a dashboard as a decision the group made, they stay a readable length, and decisions and next steps now come through when you typed your own notes during the meeting.

Next steps say when nobody was named. When a meeting agrees a next step without saying who will do it, the write-up no longer guesses. The step shows "Who?" with the people in the meeting to choose from, and your choice stays if you regenerate the write-up.

Fixed. Dictation now types into Tailwing's own text boxes, such as a project's description, a note or the Ask box. Exported files no longer get a doubled extension. Undo while typing undoes your typing. Deleting a folder, a template or your dictation history asks first. Dictated text placed before a word is followed by a space. Private mode's one-time model download now covers live captions. Closing setup early no longer marks it finished.

Known issues. The selected row in Decisions and in the sidebar is hard to read on the blue highlight. After a call, your own voice can show as "Speaker 1" or your email address where your name should be. Ask reads what it will assume for questions in English only. Translations of the newest wording are awaiting review by native readers. The reason shown under a decision is often missing in long meetings.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.2
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 2

Setup that finishes by itself. Tailwing now downloads every model it needs on its own, shows how far along each one is, and tries again if a download stops. Dictation works as soon as its speech model is in, with no need to reopen the app. Settings, Models and Settings, Permissions use the same rows and the same words, and each opens with one line that says whether everything is ready.

Private mode from the first screen. If you choose Private mode during setup, Tailwing downloads its models once and then stays offline. If a model is missing later, Settings, Models says so and offers Download Once, which leaves Private mode on.

Better write-ups of long meetings. In meetings of 35 minutes and more, Tailwing now catches far more of the decisions and next steps, including the ones made late in the meeting.

One document for your notes. Your own lines stay as you wrote them, and the write-up fills in around them. Anything you type after the write-up is included the next time it's written. Exports, the folder and webhook files, the local API and AI tools all get the same document, and the local API marks which lines are yours.

A redesigned side panel. During a call it shows your notes with a strip of the transcript. After the call it shows the write-up, with Notes, Transcript and Ask a tap away.

Dictation can read your browser tab. In Chrome, Arc, Edge or Brave, dictation can also spell the names on the page you're typing into. It's off until you turn on "Also use the page in your browser tab" in Settings, Dictation. macOS asks to let Tailwing control your browser, which Tailwing uses only to check that no private window is open before it reads. Safari can't tell Tailwing whether a private window is open, so Tailwing never reads Safari pages.

Better speaker names on calls. When an invite lists the people on a call, it now limits how many voices Tailwing assigns to your microphone, so a short burst of speech is less likely to become an extra speaker. A name that sounds close to yours isn't offered as someone else, and a voice that thanks or greets someone is no longer taken to be that person.

Also new. Check for Updates is in the menu-bar menu. Speech runs on the Neural Engine by itself for English meetings on Macs that have one. Clearer wording across Settings and setup.

Fixed. Dictation keeps going if your input device changes while you hold the key. Dictation no longer pastes into a field that can't be described while a password field is in use elsewhere. Dictation never waits more than a second for names from the screen.

Known issues. Page reading in Arc, Edge and Brave has had only light testing. Translations of the newest wording are awaiting review by native readers. Features that use your own voice are not part of this beta.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.1
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 1

A new start. Setup walks through the six things Tailwing does, one at a time: meeting notes, asking your meetings, dictation, privacy, your tools and languages. Each step asks for its permission where it's needed.

Encrypted on your Mac, audio included. Notes and transcripts were already encrypted on this Mac. Meeting audio is now encrypted as soon as the meeting is written up. A recovery code lets you open your notes on a new Mac after Migration Assistant or a restore from a backup; it's in Settings, Privacy, Your data.

AI tools are back. Claude and other AI tools read your meetings through the Tailwing app again, and only while you allow it: turn them on in Settings, Connections, AI tools.

Calls end better. When a call goes quiet, Tailwing asks before it stops. If a browser call it stopped picks up again, it asks whether to continue the last meeting.

Anonymize. The Pro feature that replaces names and personal details before anything leaves your Mac is now called Anonymize.

Coming next: more accurate dictation that spells the names on your screen, and sharper notes. Tell us what to fix first with Send Feedback in the Tailwing menu.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.8.2
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 8.2

Notes now stop by themselves when a browser call ends. After a Meet in Chrome, Tailwing could go on taking notes until you stopped it: Chrome kept hold of the microphone, and a normal room is rarely quiet enough for Tailwing to decide the call was over.

This version watches the same signal as the orange microphone dot in your menu bar, so leaving the call ends notes within seconds. If you were only stepping away, the call taking the microphone again within two minutes picks up the same meeting.

The AI tools connector is still paused, as in RC 8.1. It comes back in the next release.
